standard.--help: Shows help for the selected command and exits.
standard.--completions: Prints a shell completion script for the named shell and exits.

commands.agent-hop: Moves a Codex or Claude Code CLI session between the two workstations.
commands.agent-hop run: Starts a managed native agent session that can transfer execution.
commands.agent-hop move: Queues a managed agent handoff after its active work reaches a safe boundary.
commands.agent-hop status: Shows the recorded ownership and handoff state of a managed run.
commands.agent-hop cancel: Cancels a queued move before ownership transfers.
commands.agent-hop follow: Attaches to the destination that owns the moved agent.
commands.agent-hop recover: Resolves execution ownership before recovering a managed agent.
commands.doc-purge: Purges comments, doc strings and typographic glyphs from source files.
commands.dotfile: Manages this repository's symlinks, packages, themes, secrets, and system files.
commands.dotfile add: Moves a live config into the repository and symlinks it back.
commands.dotfile remove: Moves a tracked path out of the repository and keeps it live.
commands.dotfile sync: Refreshes generated metadata and reconciles `$HOME` with a selected profile.
commands.dotfile dev check: Runs the selected linters and test suites.
commands.dotfile doctor: Checks dotfiles health: profile's links, required tools, and packages.
commands.dotfile secret: Keeps private material out of the repository.
commands.dotfile secret scan: Scans for leaked tokens, private values, and encryption invariants.
commands.dotfile secret init: Creates this machine's age identity and prints its public key.
commands.dotfile secret enroll: Adds a recipient or enrolls this machine when no key is provided.
commands.dotfile secret revoke: Removes a recipient and gives every encrypted file a new data key.
commands.dotfile secret roll: Replaces a recipient's key while keeping its label.
commands.dotfile secret rekey: Gives every encrypted file a new data key without changing recipients.
commands.dotfile secret doctor: Checks identities, recipients, hooks, and encrypted files.
commands.dotfile secret add: Encrypts a live file into the repository and keeps it in place.
commands.dotfile secret edit: Opens a tracked secret in `$EDITOR` and reapplies it.
commands.dotfile secret apply: Decrypts every tracked secret to its destination.
commands.dotfile secret status: Shows what each tracked secret looks like on this machine.
commands.dotfile secret vars: Lists the names that secret templates can reference.
commands.dotfile secret clean: Removes materialized secrets from their destinations.
commands.dotfile system: Tracks root-owned files under `/etc` and installs them as root.
commands.dotfile system status: Compares tracked system files with their installed versions.
commands.dotfile system diff: Shows what would change on disk without modifying anything.
commands.dotfile system install: Installs tracked system files at their destinations as root.
commands.dotfile system add: Copies a root-owned file into the repository.
commands.dotfile theme: Stamps selected theme profiles into generated configuration files.
commands.dotfile theme sync: Regenerates every config from the selected theme profiles.
commands.dotfile theme dry: Reports what theme generation would change without writing.
commands.dotfile theme status: Shows each group's resolved profile and whether generated files have drifted.
commands.dotfile theme preview: Previews a profile's palette, roles, fonts, and terminal colors.
commands.dotfile theme gallery: Shows the shared picker, progress, and comparison components using a theme profile.
commands.dotfile theme switch: Assigns a profile globally, to a group, or to a package.
commands.dotfile theme check: Validates every profile and resolved application color pair.
commands.dotfile theme contrast: Prints one or every profile's resolved contrast matrix.
commands.dotfile theme outputs: Prints the files owned by the theme generator.
commands.dotfile-format: Formats a tree by handing each language to the tool that owns it.
commands.dotfmt: Formats the `.conf`, `.config`, and `.dotfile` files in a tree.
commands.flatten: Lifts a directory's contents out of the directories holding them.
commands.gdd: Discards tracked and untracked working-tree changes while preserving ignored files and nested repositories.
commands.gget: Downloads a file or directory from a GitHub repository into the current directory.
commands.gppf: Stages everything, commits with the supplied message, and pushes the commit.
commands.hpull: Copies a path from the other machine to the same place on this one.
commands.hpush: Copies a path from this machine to the same place on the other one.
commands.hwire: Inspects connections or measures latency and throughput between two machines.
commands.hwire serve: Answers measurements until told to stop.
commands.mux-route: Prints the WezTerm mux domain for the best route to the peer.
commands.path: Prints the repository-relative or home-relative path of a target.
commands.size: Reports sizes and line counts for files and directories.
commands.sysinfo: Summarizes the current machine's environment and hardware.
commands.sysinfo bench: Opens the benchmark command menu or prints its help.
commands.sysinfo bench run: Measures the current machine and optionally stores the result.
commands.sysinfo bench health: Reports warnings derived from benchmark history.
commands.sysinfo bench trend: Shows one benchmark metric over time.
commands.sysinfo bench baseline: Sets, clears, or shows the baseline run for a machine and hardware configuration.
commands.sysinfo bench prune: Removes superseded runs while preserving baselines and configuration history.
commands.transcript: Archives AI agent sessions as Obsidian notes.
commands.transcript capture: Wraps clipboard text as a transcript note in the vault.
commands.transcript import: Imports a Claude Code or Codex session as a transcript note.
commands.transcript list: Lists recent Claude Code and Codex sessions.
commands.transcript add: Tracks a project for transcript sync.
commands.transcript rm: Stops tracking a project while preserving its existing notes.
commands.transcript migrate: Moves existing transcript groups to their configured destinations.
commands.transcript sync: Syncs allowlisted Claude Code and Codex sessions into the vault.
commands.dotfile docs: Generates and checks CLI reference, keybindings, package documentation, and README previews.

agent-hop.--dry-run: Reports what would be copied and started without changing either machine.
agent-hop.--no-connect: Copies the session without opening it on the other workstation.
agent-hop.--list: Prints the local and remote sessions as tab-separated rows instead of opening the picker.
agent-hop.--resume: Starts a managed run from this agent conversation ID.
agent-hop.--pane: Selects a managed tmux pane; defaults to the current pane.
agent-hop.--to: Selects `archie` or `macie` as the execution destination.
agent-hop.--run: Selects a durable managed-run ID instead of a tmux pane.

count.--recursive: Counts every entry below the directory instead of only its direct children.
count.--no-hidden: Excludes hidden entries and everything inside hidden directories.

dotfile.--jobs: Limits the total worker budget; defaults to CPU count.
dotfile.--concurrency: Limits simultaneous development tasks; defaults to two.
dotfile.--python-workers: Caps Python workers within the total worker budget; defaults to four.
dotfile.--changed: Selects affected packages and dependents from working changes or --changed=REF.
dotfile.--shared: Places an added file in the shared package group.
dotfile.--linux: Places an added file in the `linux/common` package group.
dotfile.--arch: Places an added file in the `linux/arch` package group.
dotfile.--ubuntu: Places an added file in the `linux/ubuntu` package group.
dotfile.--kde: Places an added file in the `linux/kde` package group.
dotfile.--hyprland: Places an added file in the `linux/hyprland` package group.
dotfile.--server: Places an added config in the `linux/server` package group.
dotfile.--macos: Places an added file in the `macos` package group.
dotfile.--pkg: Selects development targets or names an added config, secret, or system package.
dotfile.--dry-run: Plans without changing files or contacting the peer.
dotfile.--force: Resolves local edits from the repository and discards remote edits with `--push`.
dotfile.--resolve: Chooses `skip`, `repo`, or `live` for locally edited merged configs.
dotfile.--push: Pushes commits, then pulls and syncs the peer.
dotfile.--verbose: Shows detailed sync actions or live development commands, output, and timings.
dotfile.--all: Shows every finding or file location instead of summarized output.
dotfile.--staged: Scans the content staged for commit.
dotfile.--review: Inspects findings and remembers accepted file contents locally; changed contents need review again.
dotfile.--commits: Scans blobs added within revision-list ranges; repeat to combine ranges into one review.
dotfile.--no-canaries: Skips the private-value tier of secret scanning.
dotfile.--using: Uses the selected identity file for recipient and re-encryption operations.
dotfile.--rewrap: Updates the recipients on every encrypted file during secret sync.
dotfile.--marker: Forces the `.secret` package marker on or off.
dotfile.--unused: Lists only variable names that no secret template references.
dotfile.--yes: Installs system files without asking for confirmation.
dotfile.--group: Selects the package group for an added system file.
dotfile.--only: Selects documentation outputs; repeat or comma-separate.
dotfile.--check: Reports stale documentation without writing; exits 1 on drift or missing metadata.

doc-purge.--type: Limits the walk to one file type, named by extension or by language, and repeats or takes a comma-separated list for several.
doc-purge.--dry: Shows what would go without writing anything.
doc-purge.--verbose: Lists every row instead of truncating sections after 12 rows.

dotfile-format.--check: Verifies formatting and runs each language's linter instead of writing anything.
dotfile-format.--add: Offers this repository's tool configuration to the target, asking per file.
dotfile-format.--sync: Replaces the tool configuration the target already has, without asking.
dotfile-format.--verbose: Names every file as it is formatted.

dotfmt.--check: Reports files that are not formatted instead of rewriting them.
dotfmt.--stdin: Formats standard input as the named file and writes the result to standard output.
dotfmt.--owns: Reads NUL-separated paths from standard input and answers with the ones it formats.
dotfmt.--verbose: Names every file as it is formatted.

flatten.--deep: Brings every nested entry to the top instead of removing only wrappers.
flatten.--dry-run: Shows what would happen without changing the directory.
flatten.--verbose: Names every move as it is made.
flatten.--all: Lists every row instead of truncating sections after 12 rows.

git.--dry-run: Shows what `gdd` would discard without changing the working tree.
git.--all: Makes `gdd` list every entry instead of truncating its sections, and includes dotfiles in a `gget` listing.
git.--list: Prints the contents of the `gget` target instead of downloading it.
git.--yes: Skips confirmation before discarding changes or replacing a download.
git.--fredrir: Reads the `gget` target as a repository owned by `fredrir`.
git.--branch: Selects the branch or tag from which `gget` downloads.

home-copy.--dry-run: Reports what would be transferred and changes nothing.
home-copy.--checksum: Compares file contents instead of size and modification time.
home-copy.--all: Includes files that .gitignore, .git, and the shared exclude list would otherwise skip.
home-copy.--yes: Accepts the mirrored location without opening the browser or asking.
home-copy.--verbose: Lists every transferred path instead of counting them.
home-copy.--to: Sets the directory on the other machine to copy into.
home-copy.--from: Sets the path on the other machine to copy out of.

hwire.--route: Selects the cable, Wi-Fi, LAN, or Tailscale route to measure.
hwire.--time: Sets the transfer duration for each direction.
hwire.--streams: Sets the number of concurrent transfer connections.
hwire.--samples: Limits the number of round trips timed.
hwire.--latency: Measures round-trip latency without running transfers.
hwire.--up: Transfers only from this machine to the peer.
hwire.--down: Transfers only from the peer to this machine.
hwire.--at: Measures an already-running server without starting one over SSH.
hwire.--token: Uses or requires the server's authentication token.
hwire.--info: Shows the current connection or the routes available to the peer.
hwire.--verbose: Shows detailed information, with an animated view on a terminal.
hwire.--watch: Refreshes connection information as routes change.
hwire.--interval: Sets the refresh interval for watched connection information.
hwire.--notify: Rings the terminal bell when the preferred route changes.
hwire.--json: Prints connection information or measurements as JSON.
hwire.--bind: Sets the address on which `hwire serve` listens.
hwire.--port: Sets the server port, with zero selecting an available port.
hwire.--idle: Sets how long an idle server waits before exiting.

mux-route.--list: Prints every route with its state, peer address, and domain instead of one domain.

path.--full: Prints the full path instead of a relative one.

size.-r: Lists the immediate contents of the directory.
size.-R: Lists the contents of the directory recursively.
size.--apparent: Measures logical lengths rather than the space actually taken up.
size.--limit: Limits how deep the recursive listing goes.
size.--all: Includes hidden entries in listings, which totals count either way.
size.--ignore: Leaves matching entries out of both the listing and the totals.
size.--one-file-system: Stays on the filesystem the target sits on, leaving other mounts out.

sysinfo.--pretty: Shows the complete branded hardware presentation.
sysinfo.--tier: Selects the quick, standard, or heavy benchmark tier.
sysinfo.--only: Limits a run to a comma-separated list of measurement families.
sysinfo.--note: Records why a benchmark run was taken.
sysinfo.--tag: Adds a label to a benchmark run.
sysinfo.--host: Selects the host to record, list, assess, or prune.
sysinfo.--workdir: Selects the directory used by the disk benchmark tier.
sysinfo.--force: Runs benchmarks despite unsuitable measurement conditions.
sysinfo.--no-save: Prints a benchmark result without storing it.
sysinfo.--baseline: Pins the new benchmark run as its machine's baseline.
sysinfo.--json: Emits a run or comparison as JSON.
sysinfo.--limit: Limits the number of stored runs listed.
sysinfo.--all: Includes noisy and aborted runs in a listing.
sysinfo.--keep: Sets the number of runs retained per machine configuration.
sysinfo.--dry-run: Reports which runs would be pruned without deleting them.
sysinfo.--yes: Prunes stored runs without asking for confirmation.

transcript.--raw: Skips secret redaction during capture, import, or sync.
transcript.--quiet: Prints nothing after a successful capture or sync.
transcript.--fallback: Selects a snapshot file when the clipboard is empty.
transcript.--limit: Sets how many sessions appear in the import picker or session list.
transcript.--tools: Includes tool calls in imported or synchronized notes.
transcript.--name: Sets the tracked project name instead of deriving it from the directory.
transcript.--group: Assigns a tracked project to a transcript group.
transcript.--verbose: Lists every file in the migration preview.
transcript.--dry-run: Reports sync changes without writing them.
